ledger.claim: The rider's own chat message asked the driver to stop at Jurong Point first, and the driver agreed. Under POL-RD-04 the deviation is exonerated to the extent it is attributable to that rider instruction, so the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor must be excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

The rider instruction satisfies POL-RD-04(a) to (c): it came from the rider (MSG-02811-001, sender RIDER), it was sent at 06:33:18, only 60 seconds after the meter started at 06:32:18 and well before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and it names a specific place, 'Jurong Point', carried as a resolved waypoint_hint at lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726.

The gps_trace corroborates the instruction as POL-RD-04 requires: the vehicle passes within 21.70 m of the requested waypoint at fix index 104, timestamped 2026-08-17T06:49:38, far inside the 200 m threshold set by POL-RD-04. The corroboration test is therefore satisfied and the clause is available.

The rider's claim that this was 'a tour' rather than a quick stop is contradicted by the record: the only waypoint the trace approaches is the one the rider herself named, and the driver's counterparty statement that 'the rider asked for the stop, it is in the chat' is borne out by the chat log. The rider cannot recover for a detour she requested.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has shown the artifacts describe the same trip with matching trip identifier TRP-02811 across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and an excess of 6.09 km / 30.0% over the 20.3 km optimal. That shifts the burden to the driver, and the driver has discharged it by pointing to the chat_log and POL-RD-04.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 207 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met and the deviation is measured on the trace as recorded rather than on any impaired stretch.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: the only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no external traffic cause can reduce the excess. ledger.claim: The fare is METERED, not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route and POL-RD-02 is the operative arithmetic clause. The recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is 27.4970 against a charged_total of 34.00, a refund of 6.5030, which rounds up to 6.55 payable and is above the 0.50 de minimis.

The refund under POL-RD-02 is 6.5030, which is 19.13% of charged_total and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND and not a FULL_REFUND. The rider is not entitled to the whole 34.00.

No ERP or toll line is in dispute: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and a zero tolls_erp figure, so POL-RD-09 pass-through corrections add nothing to the rider's recovery and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 348 is 0.0029, below the 0.05 ratio. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral is licensed on this record.

The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so the claim is not one that requires corroboration beyond the gps_trace. The rider's claim is nonetheless defeated on the merits by the rider-requested detour, not by her filing history.

The rider's claim that she 'only asked for a quick stop, not a tour' is not supported by the record on the distance she contests: the excess of 6.09 km is the distance to and from the waypoint she named, and POL-RD-04 excludes exactly that stretch. To the extent the rider seeks the full 9.00 contested, the record does not support it and that part of the claim should be rejected.

The rider's own chat message asked for the stop: 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', sent at 06:33:18, one minute after the meter started and before the vehicle left the optimal corridor. The driver agreed ('ok'). This is a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log that meets POL-RD-04(a) and (b).

The gps_trace corroborates the requested waypoint: the vehicle's nearest fix to the Jurong Point waypoint resolved from the chat message (waypoint_hint lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726) is 21.70 m away, well inside the 200 m threshold set by POL-RD-04. The corroboration test is therefore satisfied on the record, not undecidable.

The excess the rider complains of is 6.09 km / 30.0% over the booked optimal of 20.3 km, measured on a clean 100% coverage trace with 207 fixes at a 10 s interval and no gaps. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so the deviation is established on the trace itself and no independent corroboration is required.

The rider's instruction was specific enough to act on and was given before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, so the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. The rider asked for the detour and cannot now be refunded for the distance it cost.

The driver's traffic excuse is not needed and is not relied on: the bundle holds no traffic_advisory covering this trip window (EV-ADVIS-02811-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0), so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and no external-cause exoneration is asserted. The rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 is the driver's ground, and it is a ground the record supports.

ruling.explanation:
Decision for trip TRP-02811. Both parties are told the same thing: the record shows the rider asked for the stop, so the fare she contests stands.

What was measured. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02811) ran 26.39 km against a 20.3 km platform optimal, an excess of 6.09 km, or 30.0%. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 100% coverage, 207 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and the excess is established on the trace under POL-RD-01. It is below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises.

Why no refund is due. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02811) contains the rider's own message at 06:33:18 — 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something' — sent one minute after the meter started at 06:32:18, that is before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, followed by the driver's 'ok'. The waypoint_hint the platform resolved from that message (lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726) is corroborated by the trace: the nearest fix is 21.70 m away, well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold. All three conditions of POL-RD-04(a) to (c) are therefore met — the instruction was the rider's, was timely, and named a specific place — and the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor, which is the detour to and from Jurong Point, is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. With that stretch removed no excess is left to found a deviation, the driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 shifts to him by pointing to the chat_log and POL-RD-04, and POL-RD-01 gives NO_ACTION.

The rider's objection that this was 'a tour' is not supported. The only waypoint the trace approaches is the one the rider herself named, and the 6.09 km is the distance to it and back. The driver's statement that the rider asked for the stop is confirmed by the chat and the trace, not merely asserted.

The arithmetic offered for the rider does not issue. Charged_total was 34.00, and a recomputation against the booked 20.3 km / 27.4 min optimal would give a recomputed_fare of 27.4970, a difference of 6.5030 and a rounded 6.55. POL-RD-02 runs only against the adjusted optimal, and here the adjustment removes the whole excess, so no distance-or-time refund arises for the rider and the 0.50 de minimis question never falls to be asked.

Other lines. The fare is METERED with zero ERP and toll lines, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and there is no billing-integrity referral. The rider was billed 26.4 km against a 26.39 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall and no DRIVER_COMPENSATION. Neither profile decides anything about this trip: deviation_flags_90d is 1 over 348 completed trips, below both POL-RD-06 tests, and deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the POL-RD-08 threshold; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter was flagged as context-only and is not used.

Two claims about the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02811-01, weight 0.0) were discarded by the referee for not naming the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code and are not reinstated; in any event no party asserts an external traffic cause here, so no advisory is needed and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

Result. The present state stands: the 34.00 charge is not refunded and no compensation is paid. The monetary effect is 0, below the 8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes on issue, and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04. Confidence is 0.90, capped by the full-weight artifacts (EV-CHAT-02811, EV-GPS-02811) that carry the deciding fact.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
